answer: Persistent Reputation Ripple: each identity carries a slowly decaying history of its interactions. New identities start with near-zero trust, so duplicate accounts cannot immediately bridge into trust-weighted flows. Each successful transaction emits a ripple that only accumulates over time. To fake N credible identities, an attacker must sustain real activity on every one for the full decay window, paying N times the ongoing transaction cost, while a prism of cross-checks flags correlated timing.
